Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when hypertension may be present, but they don't provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they require periodic calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trial results involving thousands of participants...

Silent killer

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) both pose serious health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous and is even known as the "silent killer" — it can cause serious and irreversible damage to arteries, the heart and the brain without any obvious symptoms. Many people only discover they have the condition after suffering a heart attack or stroke.

For older adults, regular blood pressure measurement is ideal. There are many easy-to-use home upper-arm blood pressure monitors on the market. However, a fitness device that can be worn all day and monitor automatically would be even more ideal.

Apple Watch blood pressure feature

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models don't provide any readings — they only send alerts when signs of possible high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require periodic calibration using readings from an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring requires no calibration yet offers accuracy comparable to traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitors.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg that he nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure — an experience that motivated him to start the company.

The Signal Ring will begin taking pre-orders later today, ship in October, and cost $399 with no subscription required. The companion mobile app can display real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown in the image above).

Worth noting: the Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), although clinical trials have shown it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss isn't particularly keen on marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says the feature is best suited for older adults and people assessed by a doctor as being at risk of high blood pressure — remarks that suggest the Signal Ring may be mediocre in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
